name: Wildfire
description: Wildfire, power shutoff and smoke for exercises: the terms and sequence fire agencies, sheriffs, emergency managers and utilities use, the products they issue (incident summaries, zone-based evacuation notices, road and shelter boards, shutoff notices, smoke advisories), the decisions they make and the clocks they are measured on. Includes perimeter and spread maps with evacuation zone status, circuit and customer boards, AQI series, and simulated fires. Red flag warnings and fire weather come from the weather toolkit; floods after a fire from the flooding toolkit. Stays at coordination level: it carries no fireline tactics.
outsideParties: the National Weather Service forecast office and its fire weather desk
the interagency dispatch or coordination center
the electric utility's public safety partner liaison

advisorRoles.name: Fire behavior analyst (planning section)
advisorRoles.description: Explains the projected arrival at each zone, what the projection assumes and how it changes with the wind.

advisorRoles.name: Utility wildfire mitigation lead
advisorRoles.description: Knows the circuits, the shutoff criteria, the notification windows and the customers who rely on power.

advisorRoles.name: Smoke and air quality advisor (public health)
advisorRoles.description: Explains the AQI categories, clean-air shelters and what schools and events usually decide.

metrics.label: Evacuation order before the latest time to give it (arrival less clearance time; series in minutes past that time)
De-energization decision before gusts reach the circuit threshold (series in mph above the threshold)
School or facility action when the AQI crosses 150 (a local plan threshold; edit per project)

decisionForms.label: Issue an evacuation order
decisionForms.description: Leave now, for a zone picked from the list or drawn on the map. The scenario scores the order against the fire's projected arrival less the zone's clearance time.

decisionForms.label: Issue an evacuation warning
decisionForms.description: Be ready to leave, for a zone picked from the list or drawn on the map.

decisionForms.label: Order shelter in place
decisionForms.description: Stay inside, for a zone or a facility.

decisionForms.label: Open a shelter
decisionForms.description: A shelter for people or animals.

decisionForms.label: Close or control a road
decisionForms.description: A closure, a traffic control point or contraflow.

decisionForms.label: Request resources or mutual aid
decisionForms.description: Engines, crews, aircraft or other help.

decisionForms.label: De-energize or re-energize a circuit
decisionForms.description: The shutoff decision for a circuit, scored against the wind event window.

decisionForms.label: Send a shutoff notification
decisionForms.description: A notice to partners or customers, scored against the notification windows.

decisionForms.label: Record contact with medical baseline customers
decisionForms.description: Attempts and confirmed contacts for a circuit, entered by the facilitator.

decisionForms.label: Notify a critical facility
decisionForms.description: A hospital, care home, water pump or cell site.

decisionForms.label: Activate a community resource center
decisionForms.description: A site that offers charging, water and information during a shutoff.

decisionForms.label: Close a school or move a facility
decisionForms.description: A school, hospital, care home or venue acting on smoke or fire. Scored against the AQI threshold crossing.

decisionForms.label: Issue a smoke advisory
decisionForms.description: A public health advisory for the affected areas.

glossary.term: Evacuation order, warning, shelter in place
glossary.definition: Local officials issue them and the words vary by place, so use the project's own definitions. A common pattern: order means leave now, warning means be ready to leave.
A mapped polygon at one time; between maps the edge is not known, so never present minute-by-minute truth.
Percent of the perimeter with a control line expected to hold. It is not size and it can fall.
A utility turns off power on circuits in high wind and dry fuels to avoid starting a fire. Medical baseline customers rely on power and get extra notice.
Good 0.0-9.0; Moderate 9.1-35.4; Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups 35.5-55.4; Unhealthy 55.5-125.4; Very Unhealthy 125.5-225.4; Hazardous 225.5+.
1 to 5; at 5 resources are below drawdown levels for multiple resource types.

productConventions: Zone ids and status words (evacuation order, evacuation warning, shelter in place, none) are the same on the map, in the zone table and in every message; each message names the zones it addresses.
Alerts reuse cap_alert, eas_broadcast and incident_alert_notification; red flag and fire weather products come from the weather toolkit.
Size is acres with the time it was mapped; containment is a percent; times are local with a time zone.
Shutoff notice windows (an example rule, edit per project): partners 48-72 hours ahead, customers 24-48 hours, 1-4 hours if possible, and at de-energization.
Name shelters and sites by building (a school gym), never a real street address.
realismRules: Sheriffs and police issue evacuation orders; the fire agency requests them.
An order should go out before the fire's arrival at the zone less its clearance time; the arrival is the scenario's projection, not a prediction.
A wind shift changes which zones are threatened first.
Count attempts and contacts to medical baseline customers separately; only a confirmed contact is a reached customer.
School and event AQI thresholds are local plans, not federal rules.
Agencies, people, circuits and customers are fictional; a real fire appears only as dated history.

criticalTasks: Give evacuation orders and warnings before the fire reaches a zone less its clearance time.
Use the same zone ids and status words on the map, the table and every message.
Send each shutoff notice inside its window and say what customers should do.
Issue smoke advisories with the AQI category name and local guidance.
Reach zones through more than one channel and use sweeps where alerts cannot reach.
Correct a wrong or missed zone message on every channel at once.
Share the zone map and projected arrival between fire, sheriff and emergency management.
Coordinate the utility's shutoff with the county and the fire district before it starts.
Control roads, run contraflow and keep a route open for responders.
Move people who cannot move themselves before the order's latest time.
Open shelters for people and animals and size them for access and functional needs.
Open community resource centers and clean-air shelters when they are needed.
Decide to de-energize and re-energize circuits against the wind event window.
Protect critical facilities on circuits that lose power and track generator fuel.
Treat a perimeter as a mapped polygon at a time and date every projection.
Track size, containment and structures with their definitions and times.
State resource orders by number and status and prioritize structures when resources are short.
